result.title: Do Thinking VLMs Need to Keep Looking at Long Videos? Write It Down, Then Look Away
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) reason about long videos over hundreds to thousands of tokens. Every decoding step re-reads the key-value (KV) cache of the entire video. Must the model keep looking while it reasons? In LookAway, the model first writes timestamped notes on what the question needs and then puts the video away. Once the notes close, the inference engine hides the video's KV cache for the rest of the response. Across both hybrid and pure-attention VLMs, dependence on the video is concentrated early in the response. On Qwen3.6-27B, writing notes preserves accuracy better than free reasoning at the same withdrawal step. Replacing them with another video's notes harms accuracy, whereas keeping the video visible alongside the model's own notes adds no significant benefit. Without additional training, LookAway nearly matches full-video thinking accuracy at 0.12-0.13 times its modeled decode cost. To shorten this initial look, we fine-tune the model on its own correct LookAway responses. Reinforcement learning then rewards correct answers while penalizing KV reads. The trained model puts the video away after a median of 66-68 tokens. Across three held-out benchmarks, it writes more tokens than an identically trained full-video model yet reads only 27-35% as many KV positions at matched accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究长视频 VLM 在推理时是否必须持续读取整段视频的 KV cache，提出 LookAway：先写出带时间戳的笔记，随后在解码中隐藏视频 KV；并用自生成正确响应微调加 RL（奖励答对、惩罚 KV 读取）来缩短初始观察长度。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 LOOK/STOP 的收益与成本：指出对视频的依赖集中在回答早期，替换他人笔记会掉点而保留视频无额外收益，可核查笔记是否保留了任务必要的视觉细节、停止点如何决定以及 KV 读取与准确率的权衡。
